beats: Hook: if guessing is cheap, why guess one sentence? Guess a whole tree of them and check them all at once (line_draft_card_tree, the cover; line_draft_tree_present).

SpecInfer (slide 8): a static draft tree such as <2,2,1>; the editor keeps the longest prefix that matches any branch (red pen along the accepted path on line_draft_card_tree); LLaMA-7B target with a 68M draft.

One pass for the whole tree (slide 9): load the weights once (line_draft_heavy_dictionary), share the prefix, and a tree-shaped mask lets each word see only its own ancestors (line_draft_family_wall).
Medusa (slide 10): no separate intern; extra heads on the big model guess words +1 to +4 at once (line_medusa_parrots): the 2018 blockwise idea revived, with tree attention and speculative sampling.
Which tree? (slides 11-12) a static 64-node sparse tree grown greedily on calibration data (line_draft_gardener); broad for 7B, deep and narrow for 33B (line_draft_broad_vs_deep).
Medusa-1 freezes the big model and trains only the heads (line_medusa_ice_block); Medusa-2 trains them together and does better (line_medusa_train_together) (slide 13).
Numbers (slide 13): checking 64 tokens costs about one step at batch 1 (line_spec_oven_full_tray from L08-01 if it is in the library).
Takeaway: self-drafting works once the model is big enough; next episode: EAGLE.
Cover (line_cover_l08_02; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the intern presents a small potted tree hung with blank word tags; the editor traces one branch with his pen.

drawings.name: line_draft_card_tree
drawings.prompt: A small tree growing in a round clay pot, drawn like a clean diagram-tree: one short trunk splits into two branches, each of those splits into two more, and each of those four continues as one last short twig, so the tree has three levels; at the end of every branch and every twig hangs one small blank rectangular paper tag on a string, like a gift tag (ten tags in all). The branches are clean and well separated so a path can be traced along them later. Square image 1024x1024; the tree and pot fill about 80% of the width and about 85% of the height, centred. The tags are blank: no text, no letters, no numbers.

Landscape image 1536x1024; the tree of frames fills about 90% of the width and about 75% of the height. No name plates, no text, no letters, no numbers.

drawings.name: line_medusa_parrots

Square image 1024x1024; the editor, the perch and the parrots fill about 85% of the width and about 85% of the height. The cards are blank: no text, no letters, no numbers.

Portrait image 1024x1536; the gardener and the tree fill about 80% of the width and about 85% of the height. The notebook pages are blank: no text, no letters, no numbers.

Right: a tall, narrow tree like a slim cypress with one main stem and only short side twigs, reaching high, many levels deep. Landscape image 1536x1024; the two trees fill about 80% of the width and about 85% of the height, the right one clearly taller and the left one clearly wider. No text, no letters, no numbers.

drawings.prompt: On the left, the intern (the same invented character as in the references: small, quick and young, simple round face, dot eyes, short spiky hair, a hoodie with pushed-up sleeves, sneakers, a pencil tucked behind one ear) proudly holds out a small potted tree with both hands, presenting it like a trophy; its branches fork two or three times and a small blank paper tag hangs from the tip of every branch. On the right, the editor (the same invented character as in the references: a big, calm, older man, simple round face, dot eyes, a short bushy beard, half-moon reading glasses, a cardigan with elbow patches) leans in from his chair and traces one path from the trunk to one tag with the tip of his fountain pen, eyebrows raised, interested. The tags are blank. Landscape image 1536x1024, made as a cover picture: leave the top third of the picture completely empty, plain white (a title is lettered there later); the whole scene sits in the lower two thirds, centred, about 88% of the width wide, with a white margin on every side. Use few, large, bold, clearly separated shapes with white space between them, so the idea reads at a glance even when the picture is shown only 500 pixels wide: no small clutter, no busy background. No text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logos anywhere.
